detailed_requirements: Reserved capacity: baseline 8 GPUs (A100-equivalent) with burst pool + option to commit to 12 for peak seasons
Throughput guarantee: baseline sustained 150-200 RPS for 1k-token requests; 95th-percentile token throughput target during business hours
Latency SLOs: target p50 <= 60ms for short completions, p95 <= 200ms; strict tail percentiles for routing latency (p99 <= 350ms preferred)
Uptime target: Stormbridge requests 99.95% (max 22 minutes/month downtime). Redwood proposed 99.9% with credits; negotiating sliding scale
Credit schedule requested by Stormbridge: >=99.9% - no credit; 99.5-99.9% -> 10% monthly credit; 99.0-99.5% -> 30% credit; <99.0% -> 50% credit or termination right
Redwood counter: 99.9% SLA standard; credit tiers smaller (5% / 15% / 40%); proposed mutual termination at <98.0% over rolling 3-month period

Maintenance windows: Stormbridge wants quarterly 2-hour windows during off-peak (local 0200-0400); 30-day notice. Redwood asks for 48-72h notice and up to monthly patch windows (2 hours), plus emergency hotfixes with 2h notice

Support SLRs: Stormbridge wants P1 < 5min ack and <1hr mitigation; P2 <30min ack / <4hr mitigation; P3 <4hr ack / <24hr mitigation. Redwood proposes P1 15min/4hr, P2 1hr/8hr, P3 8hr/48hr for standard enterprise tier; asking for premium add-on for 5min P1
Routing & fallbacks: require automatic fallback to smaller model variants within same pool and cross-region failover with cold-start guarantees
Data & compliance: VPC-only control plane, KMS-backed keys, retention controls for logs, and EU residency for EU traffic

Observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route latency dashboards, and an agreed set of health metrics to calculate SLA (availability measured at API gateway level and model worker availability)
Redundancy: multi-AZ placement + pre-warmed caches to reduce tail latency; agreed warm-up cadence after deploys
